entries.0d802c88db78775a: A segment of the Product Transport Business that owns and operates car carriers and also conducts logistics business, including operation of container terminals, air and sea freight forwarding, land transport, warehousing and heavy cargo transport. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥587,887 million, accounting for most of the Product Transport Business. The automobile transport business of this segment, together with the Energy Business, contributed to the group's overall revenue growth. Demand for finished vehicle transport was firm, but vessel deployment efficiency was constrained by port congestion and the situation in the Middle East. In the port business, handling volumes at domestic container terminals were generally firm, and handling volumes at the Vietnamese terminal in which the company invests were also firm. The segment was renamed from “Car Carrier, Port & Logistics Business” in the fiscal year ended March 2026; the change has no effect on the figures.

This profit includes gains on sale of fixed assets and gains on sale of investment securities, among others. In the container ship business, the completion of newbuild vessels expanded the supply of shipping capacity, putting downward pressure on freight rates. The shipping business incurs voyage costs such as fuel, port and cargo expenses, vessel costs such as crew and ship repair expenses, and charter hire; the logistics business incurs cost of services such as labor costs.

entries.7d573100db7bb6d1: In the second stage (fiscal years 2026 to 2030) of the group management plan “BLUE ACTION 2035,” the company states it will shift the focus of management from “transformation and expansion” to “achieving results.” The three priority themes are “sharpening earning power,” “balanced capital allocation” and “building a solid management foundation,” and the key strategies are portfolio strategy, regional strategy and environmental strategy. The portfolio strategy adds a hybrid category, combining the characteristics of both, to the existing market-driven and stable-earnings categories, and aims for a diversification effect by combining businesses with different market cycles. The regional strategy designates the Indian Ocean Rim, from East Africa through South Asia to Southeast Asia, as a priority area, and the environmental strategy sets achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 as a long-term goal.

entries.a4acc831571d6cc2: A segment of the Energy Business consisting of maritime transport by crude oil tankers, product tankers, LPG carriers and chemical tankers, and the tank container business. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, crude oil tanker market conditions remained at high levels from September onward, when cargo volumes increased following the lifting of voluntary production cuts by OPEC+ countries. For product tankers, market conditions for large vessels were firm, while for LPG carriers, trade became more complex due to US port fee measures and US-China tariff issues, and ton-miles increased. For chemical tankers, market conditions softened due to uncertainty in the global economy.

entries.ac5a2c67ccdc39e0: A business that owns and operates dry bulk carriers to provide global maritime cargo transport. Principal subsidiaries are Mitsui O.S.K. Dry Bulk, Ltd., MOL OCEAN BULK PTE. LTD. and GEARBULK HOLDING AG. In January 2025, the company made Gearbulk Holding AG (Switzerland) a consolidated subsidiary. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥455,734 million (98.9% of the previous year), the third largest of the 6 business segments. Capesize bulkers saw firm shipments of iron ore and bauxite from Western Australia and Brazil, and market conditions remained solid. Panamax and smaller vessels were supported by cargo movements of grain, coal and minor bulks. In the Gearbulk open hatch vessel business, demand for transport of pulp, the main cargo, softened, but contracts were secured for transport of aluminum and project cargo. Number of employees: 328 (as of March 31, 2026).

entries.df055a3eb8a66e4c: The Dry Bulk Business transports iron ore, bauxite, coal, grain and other goods by dry bulk carriers. The Energy Business provides ocean transportation by crude oil tankers, oil product tankers, LPG carriers, chemical tankers, and LNG and ethane carriers, and also runs the FPSO offshore business and the gas infrastructure business. The Product Transportation Business transports finished vehicles by car carriers and also owns and operates container ships, operates container terminals, and runs air and ocean freight forwarding, land transportation, warehousing, heavy-cargo transportation and tank terminal businesses. The Well-being Life Business consists of real estate leasing and management of buildings and other properties, passenger and cargo transportation by ferries and domestic RORO vessels, and cruise business. The Related Business comprises towage and the sale of fuel, marine supplies and machinery, and Other comprises ship management, finance and other activities.
entries.e6da72534e1675d2: Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,825,098 million, up 2.8% from ¥1,775,470 million in the previous year. The Energy Business and the automobile transportation business contributed to the revenue increase. Revenue from external customers was ¥641,529 million for the Product Transportation Business, ¥525,793 million for the Energy Business, ¥455,734 million for the Dry Bulk Business, ¥122,298 million for the Well-being Life Business, ¥58,252 million for the Related Business and ¥21,489 million for Other. Within the Product Transportation Business, the container ship business recorded ¥53,641 million, 90.4% of the previous year's level. Ocean cargo transportation contracts are established for each voyage, and revenue is recognized as voyage days elapse. For vessel charters, the consideration for lending vessels with crew assigned and transport capacity provided is recognized at the amount that can be billed for the services provided. For LNG and ethane carriers and FPSOs in the offshore business, long-term charter contracts form the basis of revenue. Consideration for transactions is mainly received in advance based on the contractual amount.
